one_line: Ahom brothers of the 1660s who endured Mir Jumla’s Mughal invasion and then led Assam’s recovery and resistance.

appearance.age_look: Jayadhwaj appears in his late 30s to early 40s with a dignified, slightly worn build; Chakradhwaj appears late 20s to early 30s with a lean, energetic warrior’s build.
appearance.face: Both have oval faces and medium-brown Assamese complexions; Jayadhwaj has faint under-eye shadows, a short neatly trimmed moustache, and a calm, introspective default expression, while Chakradhwaj has a firmer jaw, a slightly sharper nose, a short moustache with a hint of stubble, a small old scar on his left cheek, and a determined, focused default expression.
appearance.hair: Jayadhwaj’s hair is black and gathered into a neatly tied topknot at the back of the crown, wrapped with a thin off‑white cloth band; Chakradhwaj’s black hair is pulled into a tighter, slightly higher warrior’s topknot with a narrow red band, a few loose strands falling near his temples, and neither wears metal helmets—only their cloth bands.
appearance.costume: Both wear late 17th‑century Ahom-style court-and-campaign dress: Jayadhwaj wears a long-sleeved, knee-length cotton tunic (kurta-like) in muted deep indigo blue with a simple round neck and side slits, over a cream-coloured, slightly loose dhoti wrapped to the ankles with a neat front pleat; over his shoulders is a white gamosa-style cloth with fine red woven borders and small red motifs, worn folded as a stole, and he has a narrow brown leather belt at the waist; his feet are in simple brown leather sandals and his jewellery is modest—small gold hoop earrings and a single plain gold ring on his right hand. Chakradhwaj wears a similar tunic but in earthy deep maroon-brown, slightly shorter and more fitted for movement, with a reinforced quilted texture over the chest hinting at padded protection; his dhoti is a practical light-ochre/beige, hitched slightly higher at the ankles for mobility, and he also wears a folded white gamosa with bolder red borders diagonally from his left shoulder across the torso like a sash; his belt is a slightly wider dark brown leather belt with a simple metal buckle from which hangs a small cloth pouch, and his footwear is sturdy dark-brown leather sandals. Both costumes are plain woven cotton with minimal pattern beyond the traditional red borders on the gamosa and subtle stitching details—no fantasy armour, only practical era-appropriate padding and belts.
appearance.signature: A single long Assamese-style straight-bladed sword (dao) with a slightly broad, gently tapering single-edged blade, a plain iron hilt, and a simple wooden scabbard wrapped in dark-brown leather—normally carried and gripped by Chakradhwaj, while Jayadhwaj rests his hand lightly on the scabbard to symbolise shared duty rather than wielding it.

ref_desc: Jayadhwaj Singha and Chakradhwaj Singha are medium-brown Assamese brothers with oval faces, black topknots, Jayadhwaj in deep-indigo tunic and cream dhoti, Chakradhwaj in maroon-brown padded tunic and ochre dhoti, both with white-and-red gamosa cloths and a single shared long Assamese dao in a dark-brown scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two Ahom royal brothers from 1660s Assam standing side by side: both medium-brown Assamese with oval faces, black hair in tidy topknots wrapped in cloth bands, no helmets, and serious, dignified expressions; the elder brother Jayadhwaj looks late 30s–40s, slightly worn but composed, with a short neat moustache, faint under-eye shadows, wearing a long-sleeved knee-length deep-indigo cotton tunic with side slits over a cream dhoti falling to his ankles, a narrow brown leather belt, a folded white gamosa with fine red borders over his shoulders like a stole, simple brown leather sandals, and minimal jewellery (small gold hoop earrings and a single gold ring); the younger brother Chakradhwaj looks late 20s–30s, lean and energetic, with a firmer jaw, small scar on his left cheek, short moustache and light stubble, a slightly higher warrior’s topknot tied with a narrow red band, wearing a slightly shorter, more fitted deep maroon-brown tunic with subtly quilted padding on the chest, over a light-ochre/beige dhoti hitched just above the ankles, a wider dark-brown leather belt with a simple metal buckle and small cloth pouch, a white gamosa with bold red borders worn diagonally like a sash, and sturdy dark-brown leather sandals; between them and slightly forward is one long Assamese straight-bladed dao with a plain iron hilt and wooden scabbard wrapped in dark-brown leather, held more actively by Chakradhwaj while Jayadhwaj rests a hand lightly on the scabbard, and keep the colour palette to deep indigo, maroon-brown, cream, white with red, and dark brown leather, showing them from multiple angles so their face shapes, hair, garments and shared weapon can be consistently redrawn.
